The slamming of dresser drawers and shouting roused three year old Hazel Swan from sleep.

She blinked awake slowly, eyes looking at the glow in the dark stickers her dad had put on her ceiling for her.

"No, Charlie! I've had it. I'm taking the girls and we're leaving." Her mothers voice came from right outside her bedroom. She sat up when her mother came storming in, a duffle bag behind her. "Come on, sweetie. We're going bye bye."

Bye bye?

"Renee, wait, please. Don't take the girls." Her father pleaded, following behind her mother. His hands pulling at his hair, tears gathering in his eyes.

"Daddy?" She whispered, rubbing her eyes.

"Charlie, I told you. They deserve more than this place. I deserve more."

"Babe, just hold on. Please. Give me a chance to prove to you that it'll be different. I'll work less hours, be home more. Anything."

"No, Charlie. Its been three years of the same lines. I thought after Bella... I thought... I don't know what I thought. But it wasn't this."

Renee shoved Hazel's clothes in the bag, grabbing a few toys for her as well as her blanket, but she left her favorite stuffed animal behind.

"Come on, baby. Let's go. Say bye to daddy."

Hazel waved half heartedly at her father on the porch, not quite understanding what was going on but her mom said she was going bye bye, so it couldn't be that bad. Right?

~~~~~

It had been ten years since that night.

Ten years since the Swan sisters vacated their father's home in the dead of the night.

Bella, only a few months old at the time, obviously didn't remember anything different from moving from place to place with their mother. Visiting their father during the summers and the occasional spring break. Bella was used to their mother being as scatter brained as she was. She was only seven, but even she knew there was a screw lose somewhere in Renee's brain.

Hazel, however. Had always been more intuitive than most three year olds at that age. More self aware. Always following conversations with her eyes, being able to read how someone was feeling. As she grew older, her empathy grew as well.

She was the older sibling. She was supposed to help take care of her younger sister, she was supposed to protect her. She just never realized her mother would be the one she needed to protect her from.

Unfortunately, it was a few weeks after Hazel's thirteenth birthday that Renee had decided Bella would be the easier child to look after. Less hostile and less complaining when it would come time for them to uproot their lives and leave. More pliant. The opposite of Hazel.

It was another argument between Hazel and their mother. The same old song and dance. Renee wanted to move, Hazel didn't. And she fought her harder this hard than she had before.

"You do this every time! Why can't we stay? It isn't fair." Hazel shouted, throwing her backpack on the floor behind the couch.

There were moving boxes stocked in the hallway. Again.

"Why is it so hard for you to keep a job? I don't get it."

"Watch your tone, Hazel. I am the adult here, not you." Renee replied in a stern voice. She was used to her daughters outbursts. She was as used to her defiance as she was her empathatic nature. It only seemed she had empathy towards Bella and animals nowadays. Leaving nothing left for her mother.

"Then act like one."

A hush fell over the house. Bella stopped in her tracks, her eyes going wide. She was trying to retreat to her bedroom to escape the fire that had started in Hazel the second they arrived home. Renee took a deep breath, closing her eyes to calm herself before she responded.

"I have had a enough, Hazel. If you don't want to be apart of this family and all that comes with it, then maybe you should move in with your father."

"Great. I will." Hazel trudged her way to the wall phone in the kitchen. Her eyes never leaving Renee's.

Renee crossed her arms and glared down at her daughter. Hazel was surely bluffing. Renee would just wait her out.

Hazel quickly dialed the same number she had always had memorized since she was five. When it started ringing she brought the phone to her ear.

"Good luck. I doubt he'll answer." Renee smirked. Hazel rolled her eyes and silently prayed to every God in existence that her father wouldn't let her down now.

Just when the phone was about to be picked up by the voice messaging box, Charlie answered the phone. Hazel's eyes brightened and she smiled in defiance at the shocked expression on her mother's face.

"Daddy? Can you come get me? I want to live with you."

~~~~~

The transition to Forks was easier than Hazel had anticipated. Charlie wasted no time in packing a small bag and loading up in his police cruiser and making his way south to retrieve his eldest daughter. He wished it was both of them, but Charlie knew better than to push his luck. Bella had wanted to stay with their mother, anyway.

"I, uh, wasn't expecting you to want to come back so soon. So the house is a little messy." Hazel smiled up at her father. A faint blush on his cheeks.

"It's okay, dad. I appreciate you coming to get me. Truly, you have no idea." Hazel gave him a hug, wrapping her arms around his middle and closing her eyes. Letting the scent of him wrap around her in comfort.

It wasn't that she didn't love her mother. She did.

But sometimes Hazel wondered if she were adopted for how different the two of them were.

Sure. They shared features. They had the same dirty brown hair, the same blue eyes. But where Hazel was soft, her mother was sharp. Where Hazel was kind, Renee was blunt.

Bella was always her favorite, and as the girls grew older, the favoritism was palpable. Hazel didn't understand why, she had never done anything to intentionally cause any grief from her mother. As long as she treated Bella well, that's all she cared about.

Hazel unwrapped herself from around her father and turned to enter her old bedroom.

A lot was the same from when she was a toddler. Over the years, the toddler bed had been swapped for a twin bed. The toddler and infant toys gone and the art on the walls had changed. Mostly bare, seeing as she never spent longer than a few weeks in the summer there. But it felt like home all the same.

Her comforter was a soft pink. The walls a neutral cream color, the desk in the corner was a a nice wood that matched her childhood dresser that was tucked away in the closet.

She smiled softly and placed her duffle bag on her bed. The very same duffle bag her mother had used to uproot her ten years ago in the middle of the night. The irony wasn't lost on her.

"Listen, kid. I'm glad you're here."

"Me, too, dad."

~~~~~

It was mid October when she moved back in with her father. And it was only a few weekends after she was settled when she started hanging out with Jacob Black and his sisters. More his sisters and he happened to be there. But still. She didn't complain.

It was nice to be around familiarity.

It was a month after that, when she met Paul Lahote.

She was staying the night on the reservation with Rachel and Rebecca and their mother had taken them out to get snacks and a movie from the local video store. Paul was there with Jared Cameron and Sam Uley.

Hazel had heard stories about the infamous Jared and Sam from the twins, mostly she heard about how cute they were. Seeing them now in person, she'd have to agree. But in her own opinion? Paul was the cuter one.

"Hey, Rachel, Rebecca!" Sam called, walking toward them in the horror film aisle. Jared and Paul followed behind. "Who's your friend?"

"This is Hazel! Chief Swan's daughter." Rachel introduced. Rebecca giggled from behind Hazel's shoulder. Boy crazy as ever.

"Hi, Hazel. It's nice to meet you. Uh, this is Jared and Paul."

"Hi," she said. Smiling softly at the three boys. "We're just trying to find a good movie for tonight. Any suggestions?"

"Uhh Scream is a good one!" Jared piped in. Paul scoffed.

"Yeah, if you like predictability." Paul murmured, his eyes scanning the rows of horror films.

"What are you? A horror movie critic?" Said Rachel. "The reveal was totally a plot twist." Rebecca nodded along in agreement with her sister. Sam shrugged.

The twins and Sam and Jared continued chatting about school and about the upcoming middle school Halloween dance. Hazel rolled her eyes with a soft smile on her face.

She didn't go to school with the twins. She didn't live on the reservation, she also wasn't apart of their tribe. But she never felt like an outsider.

"You're right, you know." Paul's brown eyes met Hazel's blue one. They widened just a fraction before he managed to school his features to portray indifference. But Hazel caught the light shade of pink creeping up his neck.

"Whatever." He gruffed out, crossing his arms.

"What would you suggest? I'm open to all opinions." She smiled at him and took a small step closer. "I'm more partial to Stephen King myself. But I'm willing to venture out."

Paul gave her a once over, pausing for a second before the fight left his body. He uncrossed his arms and pulled a few selection from the shelf in front of them.

"Would you prefer Dracula, or Wolf?"

~~~~~

Over the next two years, Paul and Hazel would grow closer. Any time she was with the twins, the three boys would follow. Leaving them all paired off evenly.

Rachel with Sam, Jared with Rebecca, and Hazel with Paul.

It was the new normal, and despite Hazel going to the middle school in Forks and developing her own set of friends, the would and could never replace the kind of companionship she had on the reservation.

Over time, Hazel came to think of Paul as her best friend. And he felt the same way.

Late night phone calls and every weekend spent together created a bond that they didn't think could be broken.

Hazel was the light in Paul's life. The one good thing that he felt was his. Growing up in his house, with an absent mother, he had to learn how to handle things on his own. He had his father, but he was always working long days to make ends meet. Because of this, he was unable to learn to regulate his emotions properly.

He was prone to random outbursts of anger. Often times lashing out, making him become guarded with the exception of Jared and Sam.

Hazel seemed to be the only one that could help calm his nerves. Even when he would snap at her, she would be patient with him and wouldn't leave his side. Every time he would feel guilty and apologize, but of course Hazel would forgive him every time.

At wasn't until they were fifteen when everything changed.

Sarah Black had died in a tragic car accident. Leaving the three Black siblings without a mother.

The car had been mangled so badly, that Sarah had been declared dead on scene. Police believed her to have collided with some kind of animal, causing the entire front of the car to cave in on itself.

The locals bought it, and most of those not on the reservation believed it as well.

But not Hazel.

Hazel was much like her father in a lot of ways. One of them being her dream of becoming a police officer, and one day maybe a detective. There were a lot of details about Sarah's death that didn't add up, but it wasn't as so Hazel could ask questions. She didn't want to dig into old wounds.

After the funeral, the Black twins had distanced themselves from many. Their friends at school, and even Hazel.

Sure, they still spoke. But their bond was never the same. And with the distance, Hazel's trips to the reservation became far apart. She would tag on to the occasional fishing trip to help keep Jacob occupied. But there was only so much a fifteen year old could do to help keep a nine year old distracted while the grown ups fished.

The only constant in her life after that was Paul.

Paul despite the distance, was still her rock. He would still call most evenings and after they turned sixteen, would often show up at her house on the weekends to hang out. Or sneak her away on a random drive in his Jeep.

Their time spent together was sacred.

It was during their senior year of high school when everything changed.

~~~~~

"Hey, Hazel!" Hazel turned around at the sound of her name. Her friend Anna was jogging towards her from down the hallway of Forks High.

"Hey, yourself. Why are you running? You never run." Anna rolled her eyes at her friend and leaned forward with her hands on her knees.

"Yeah and you will probably never see it happen again!" The girls laughed. Hazel grabbed the rest of her morning books and walked with Anna side by side towards their first period.

"Should have told me ahead of time so I could have prepared myself more." Hazel grinned.

"Whatever. Anyway! I was running because I wanted to intercept you before you heard from someone else."

"Heard what?"

"About the new kids!" Anna whisper yelled while collapsing into her seat in English. "There are five of them. Five! Can you believe it? Nothing this exciting ever happens here." It was Hazel's turn to roll her eyes.

"Have I ever told you how nuts you can be? But I also love you?" Anna gently swatted her on the arm.

"Shut up, gremlin. Apparently, they're the new doctors foster kids. Three of them of sophomores and two are freshmen. But after you see them, trust me you are not going to believe it."

It wasn't until lunch time did Hazel lay eyes on the new kids. And Anna was right. She didn't believe their ages.

"That guys is huge. And he's a sophomore? There's no way. He's had to have been held back." Anthony scoffed. The rest of the friends at the lunch table murmured their agreements.

"Some people are just built differently, Anthony." Hazel sighed, moving the food around her plate with her fork. Not really interested in eating as much as she was interested in the end of the day.

She needed to call Paul. She hadn't heard from him for a few days and she was getting worried. His dad had mentioned he was sick, but it wasn't like him to not call her at least once.

"Yeah, whatever, Haze."

The rest of the school day was filled with gossip and chatter about the new kids. Or The Cullens, that a freshman named Jessica Stanley had called them. Hazel didn't pay much mind to them, her mind was occupied elsewhere. Or more on someone.

Hazel rushed home in her old truck, pushing the gentle engine as quick as it could go. She had a bad feeling settle in her gut, a large knot she couldn't shake lose.

Her dad wasn't home, but that was normal these days. He spent more time at the station than he did at home. Too busy tracking giant paw prints in the nearby woods. After finding some older tracks in the woods behind the house, Hazel was on a strict curfew, and absolutely not allowed in the woods under any circumstances.

She chucked her bag on the couch in the living room and trudged her way to the wall phone in the kitchen. Dialing the all too familiar number for the Lahore household.

"Hello?" A gruff voice andwered.

"Hi, Mr. Lahore. It's Hazel. I'm really sorry to bother, but I gotta talk to Paul. Please."

Paul's dad sighed deeply before responding. "I'll ask him, Haze. But don't get your hopes up alright? He's been going through some things lately."

"I understand, sir. I just need to hear his voice." She could hear Mr. Lahote set the phone on the hook before calling for his son. A few moments went by before the familiar voice of Paul came to the line.

"What do you want, Hazel?" Hazel's eyes widened. Paul had never talked to her like that. Sure, he's been angry and has had outbursts before, but he's never been so rude like that towards her.

"I-I was just calling to make sure you were okay. I hadn't heard from you for a few days, I was hoping you were feeling better." She said in a small voice. Tangling the telephone wire around her finger.

"Yeah, well stop. Alright? I don't need to be worrying about me and looking out for me anymore."

"What's that supposed to mean?" Hazel felt a flush of anger course through her body.

"It means, I don't want to be your friend anymore. I can't be your friend anymore." He whispered. His voice tinged with regret.

"What are you talking about? We've been best friends for years, now all of a sudden you can't be my friend?" Paul sighed on the other line.

"Don't call here anymore. Okay?"

"Well, fine. I won't. Goodbye, Paul." Hazel slammed the receiver down and swiped at her face, clearing her angry tears. Several years of friendship tossed away. Like it didn't matter. Like she didn't matter.

She wished she could say she didn't know what this felt like. But she did. Maybe too well for someone her age. Mommy issues aside, Hazel wasn't going to dwell too long on someone that obviously didn't want to be in her life anymore.

~~~~~

Hazel's senior year passed without any further hiccups.

It also passed without any hint of a Paul Lahote lurking anywhere in her peripheral.

She felt the hollowness in her chest without him every day. Eventually, she was able to fill it with other things. Like time spent on the cheerleading squad. Dates with Anthony. Sleepovers with Anna and the occasional trip to the bog with Jacob to catch frogs like when they were kids.

It was also spent with more phone calls to Bella, and even less with Renee, who couldn't even be bothered to come to Hazel's graduation.

Never the less. Hazel had her father and her sister by her side. All she had been missing was her best friend.

Eventually, the hollowness in Hazel's chest became too much. After a year spent in community college in Seattle where she worked herself half to death, she was accepted early to a police academy in Meridian, Idaho for their 18-week entry-level program.

Her father was sad to see her go, but was proud of her every step of the way. And with giant paw prints showing up underneath her window in prior months, Charlie couldn't wait to send her off somewhere that would be safer for her.

Hazel packed her bags, and didn't look back at the place that had caused so much heartache.

Little did they know, that in a years time, Hazel would be back and thrown into more danger than they ever thought possible.
